title: Analytics pipeline lift-off — standup notes (2026-07-02)
content:
Date: 2026-07-02
Time: 09:15 — 09:45 PT
Attendees: Priya (owner), Ethan, Sofia, Leo, Maia (ops sync attend), Ben (data eng queued in)
Absentees: none noted

Purpose: quick mid-sprint standup focused on the analytics pipeline "lift-off" for the new Console Experiment Dashboard (CED). We need to confirm canary rollout schedule, measure instrumentation coverage, and decide on fallback behavior for the client SDK if telemetry fails.

Summary / outcomes:
- Agreed canary cohort: 5% of orgs (designated by org tag experiment:ced-canary). Launch window: 2026-07-05 00:00 PT -> rolling hourly ramp to 50% by 2026-07-07 if no regressions.
- Key KPIs to watch: event ingestion latency (95th), dashboard render TTFP, per-route sample-rate, and ingestion error rate. Dashboards created in Grafana: CED-Ingest-Latency, CED-Render-TTFP, CED-Client-Errors.
- Immediate blocker: missing server-side sampling switch in proxy (INF-3278). Ben to prioritize patch; ETA EOD 2026-07-03.

Notes (dive-in):
- Instrumentation coverage: Sofia reports ~82% of UI flows have explicit telemetry hooks (clicks, impressions, route change). Missing: nested tool panels and keyboard-only navigation events. Action: Sofia + UX to add minimal hooks for panel toggles by 2026-07-04.
- Client SDK fallback: proposal is optimistic — send telemetry via batched endpoint, fall back to noop when consecutive 5xx within 3 minutes. Leo concerns: silent noop hides user regressions. Decision: implement fallback but emit a high-priority 'client-fallback' heartbeat event to a separate (low-volume) channel so we can alert on mass client failures. Owner: Leo. Timebox: 2 days.
- Batching behaviour for low-activity orgs: current implementation waits up to 12s for batch completion. This increases TTFP for dashboards with sparse events. Proposal to add adaptive flush: if a dashboard request is active and batch is >3s old, flush immediately. Ethan to prototype; POC ready 2026-07-06.
- Dataset sampling change: Data eng suggests progressive sampling for historical events to keep storage < target. Risk: analytic discrepancy between canary and baseline. Mitigation: include sample metadata flags and expose a sampling-adjusted metric. Ben will add sampling flag to event schema (INF-3245).

Runbook / monitoring plan:
- Pager thresholds: ingestion errors >1% for 10m -> page oncall (SRE). Dashboard render TTFP 95th > 2.5s -> create incident channel and pause rollout.
- Alerting: create a temporary smoke test (every 30s) that fakes a dashboard session and asserts ingest+render path completes within 1.5s. Maia to add K8s job by 2026-07-04.
- Post-canary checklist: compare metric delta on the following windows 0-24h, 24-72h, 7d. If median metric deltas < 3% and no major errors, proceed to full rollout.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Ben: fix server-side sampling switch and add sampling flag to event schema. ETA: 2026-07-03 (blocking).
- Leo: implement client-fallback heartbeat and alert channel; add unit tests. ETA: 2026-07-04.
- Sofia: add missing UI hooks (panel toggles, keyboard nav). ETA: 2026-07-04.
- Ethan: prototype adaptive flush for client batching; benchmark TTFP impact. ETA: 2026-07-06.
- Maia: add smoke-test job (k8s). ETA: 2026-07-04.
- Priya: finalize canary cohort list (tags) and schedule rollout in Launchpad. ETA: 2026-07-03.

Risks / open questions:
- Will progressive sampling cause skewed product analytics? (Ben: mitigations via flags but data consumers need to be notified). Action: Priya to send note to growth/data consumers with expected schema change.
- Is our telemetry storage estimate still accurate if CED usage spikes? Ops: revisit capacity model after 24h of canary.
- Legal/PII: check that heartbeat/failover channel doesn't include identifiable session tokens. Security signoff pending (ticket SEC-1022).

Quick decisions made:
- Canary size 5% -> ramp plan approved.
- Client SDK fallback with heartbeat approved (Leo owner).
- Adaptive batching POC greenlit (Ethan).

Notes to self / friction points (informal):
- We should carve out a short "canary playbook" page in Confluence — lightweight checkboxes for oncall and product. Current runbook is spread across multiple pages. (Priya)
- Slack thread that tracks live metrics should be pre-populated with Grafana snapshots so the oncall on duty doesn't have to run queries. (Ethan)

Follow-ups before next standup (2026-07-03):
- Ben to update INF-3245 and confirm deploy window for server sampling switch.
- Priya to create Launchpad rollout and ping growth/data owners.
- Leo to post initial client fallback PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/987

References / links:
- Canaries doc: Confluence (link above)
- Related Jira: INF-3245 (sampling schema), INF-3278 (proxy sampling switch)
- GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/987 (client-fallback), staging dashboard branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/compare/feature/ced-staging

End notes: concise and focused — this was shorter than the rollout huddles last sprint, but we still have a few high-impact blockers. Next sync will be quick check at 09:15 2026-07-03 to confirm Ben/Leo progress and finalize Launchpad entry.

----
Raw scratch (keeps):
- "If we see ingestion lag > 500ms, lower sample-rate to 10% automatically?" -> think through data skew first.
- Check whether the SDK's batching TTL is configurable via a runtime flag so we don't require redeploys for tuning.
summary: Standup that sets canary plan, identifies blockers (server sampling switch), decides client fallback heartbeat, tasks assigned with near-term ETAs, and outlines monitoring/runbook for CED analytics lift-off.
